blocks.text: Many popular platforms use cloud computing to provide everyday digital services. Amazon Web Services (AWS) offers a wide range of cloud-based services for web hosting, data storage, and application development, widely used by businesses around the world. Microsoft Azure provides similar capabilities, enabling developers to create and manage applications through the cloud (as shown in Figure 8.4).

These platforms show how cloud computing supports various activities, from personal file storage to large-scale enterprise solutions. Whether it is saving documents, hosting websites, or running software remotely, cloud computing has become an essential part of modern digital infrastructure.

blocks.alt: Left, a USERS / CLIENTS column (Laptop, Smartphone, Tablet, Desktop) linked through an INTERNET cloud to three stacked layers: CLOUD SERVICE LAYER (SaaS, PaaS, IaaS), CLOUD MANAGEMENT LAYER (Resource Management, Monitoring, Security, Billing / Accounting, Scaling) and CLOUD INFRASTRUCTURE LAYER (Servers, Storage, Database, Networking, Data Centres). Right, a DEPLOYMENT MODELS cloud (Public, Private, Hybrid and Community Cloud) linked to the layers.
blocks.caption: Figure 8.4: Cloud Computing enables users to store, access, and share data from anywhere through the internet. (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 8.4)
blocks.long_description: Service layer: SaaS (Software as a Service), e.g., Gmail, Office 365; PaaS (Platform as a Service), e.g., Google App Engine; IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service), e.g., Virtual Machines. Arrows lead down from the service layer to the management layer and on to the infrastructure layer.
